patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Attends daycare three times per week.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: No fever, rash in other locations, itching, or systemic symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the pediatric patient presenting with multiple skin lesions.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Doctor: “Hello. What brings you in today?” Patient: “I’m here because my mom noticed small, painless bumps on my belly.”
Doctor: “How old is the patient?” Patient: “I’m 2 years old.”
Do the bumps have a small central dimple or indentation?
Doctor: “Do the bumps have a small central dimple or indentation?” Patient: “Yes, some of them have a little dent in the middle.”
How long have these bumps been present?
“These bumps have been there for about a week.”
Have the bumps spread to other areas of the body or increased in number since you first noticed them?
Patient: “Yes, they’ve spread a bit to my arms and legs, and there seem to be more of the bumps than when they first started.”
Has your child had any fever, itching, or seemed otherwise unwell?
“No, I haven’t had any fever or itching, and I’ve been acting pretty normal—no one says I seem sick.”
[DDX] Molluscum contagiosum, Varicella, Papular urticaria, Folliculitis, Viral exanthem
